This page details upcoming changes to Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) fulfillment fees.

Important: As of April 17, 2026, a 3.5% fuel and logistics-related surcharge applies to fulfillment fees across Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) in the US and Canada, as well as to Remote Fulfillment with FBA from the US into Canada, Mexico, and Brazil. As of May 2, 2026, this surcharge also applies to Buy with Prime in the US and Multichannel Fulfillment (MCF) in the US and Canada. We'll keep reviewing the surcharge as conditions change.

Holiday peak fulfillment fees apply from October 15, 2026, to January 14, 2027, for FBA, Remote Fulfillment with FBA into Canada and Mexico, Multichannel Fulfillment (MCF), and Buy with Prime. The fuel and logistics-related surcharge applies to these fees.

The Revenue Calculator, Profit Analytics dashboard, and Fee and Economics Preview reports have all been updated to reflect the peak rates and surcharge and are available to help you understand the specific impact to your business.

Effective January 15, 2027, fulfillment fees will revert to non-peak fee rates, with the following changes:

Standard-size Products:

Standard-size products priced between $10 to $50: Small standard-size product fulfillment fees for products priced between $10 to $50 will increase by $0.40 on average, and large standard-size product fees will increase by $0.12 per unit on average.
Standard-size products priced above $50: Small standard-size product fulfillment fees for products priced above $50 will increase by $0.70 on average, and large standard-size product fees will increase by $0.47 on average.
Low-price products:
Standard-size products priced below $10: Small standard-size product fulfillment fees in this price range will increase by $0.20 per unit, on average. Large standard-size product fees for non-apparel categories will remain unchanged while apparel will see increases by $0.08 per unit, on average. For more details, go to Low-price FBA fees.
Low-price Eligibility: Low-Price FBA rates will be restricted to a narrower set of fee categories. Products in the following fee categories will no longer be eligible for Low-Price FBA rates and will be charged standard rates for products priced between $10 to $50: ‘Automotive and Powersports’, ‘Compact Appliances’, ‘Musical Instruments and AV Production’, ‘Media - Books, DVD, Music, Software, Video’, and ‘Computers’. For more details, go to Low-price FBA fees.

Bulky and Extra-largeProducts:

Bulky products: We’re replacing the current small bulky and large bulky tiers with four new tiers. The current small bulky tier will be split into small bulky and medium bulky, while the current large bulky tier will be split into large bulky and extra-large bulky. Smaller and lighter products will incur lower fulfillment fees, while larger and heavier products will incur higher fees. The amount of the increase or decrease will vary based on product size and dimensions. For more information on size tiers, go to Product size tiers.
Extra-Large products: We’re replacing the current extra-large tier structure with six new oversize tiers: small oversize, medium oversize, large oversize, long oversize, special oversize light, and special oversize heavy. Smaller and lighter products will incur lower fulfillment fees, while larger and heavier products will incur higher fees. The amount of the increase or decrease will vary based on product size and dimensions. For more information on size tiers, go to Product size tiers.

Additional fees

Overmax and Oversize handling fees: Starting January 15, 2027, we’re also updating fees for irregular products, removing the Overmax handling fee, and introducing Flat product and Overhang handling fee. For more information, go to Overmax handling fee and Oversize handling fee.
Low-inventory-level fee: Effective February 1, the fee will apply only when your inventory falls below 28 days of supply, based on actual shipments in both the four weeks before and after the assessment date. By also evaluating sales in the four weeks after the inventory assessment, this change confirms whether low inventory reflects ongoing demand. It will also target SKUs that need replenishment and reduce instances triggered by unexpected demand spikes or end-of-season and end-of-life products. For more information, go to Low-inventory-level fee 2027.
Ships in Product Packaging: There are no changes to SIPP eligibility or enrollment for 2027. Ships in Product Packaging (SIPP) is a program in which products are shipped to the customer in their original packaging, without any additional packaging from us. Standard size products certified as SIPP will automatically receive lowered FBA fulfillment fees on each certified unit shipped. Bulky products that are non-certified as SIPP will see additional packaging fees. For detailed rate card, go to Ships in Product Packaging (SIPP). For details on SIPP guidelines and how to enroll, go to SIPP enrollment guidelines.

Frequently asked questions
How do I determine what product size tier my product belongs to?

To determine your product's size tier, go to Product size tiers.

Will the 2026 peak fulfillment fees apply to products ordered before October 15, 2026?

FBA fulfillment fees are calculated and charged when shipments leave fulfillment centers. If a product is ordered before October 15, 2026, but is shipped on or after that date, the peak fulfillment fees will apply.

What fulfillment fee rates apply to an item priced at exactly $10 or $50?

Items priced at $10 and $50 will be eligible for $10–$50 rates. Items priced below $10 (except select fee categories) will be eligible for <$10 rates, and items priced above $50 will be eligible for >$50 rates. For more details on items priced below $10, go to Low-price FBA fees.

Where can I preview non-peak and peak fulfillment fee?

You can preview the non-peak and peak fulfillment fee rates in the Revenue Calculator. To access the tool, go to Revenue Calculator. Additionally, you can explore the Profit Analytics tool that allows you to analyze fees, costs, and profitability for the products in your Amazon catalog.

How is dimensional weight calculated?

Dimensional weight is equal to the unit volume (length x width x height) divided by 139. For bulky items and oversize items, we assume a minimum width and height of 2 inches. We’ll use dimensional weight for fees when it is larger than the unit weight for all large-standard, bulky, and oversize (except special oversize heavy) units. Small-standard and special oversize heavy units will use unit weight for fees.

Why are over $50 fulfillment fees different from $10-50 and <$10 rates?

These rates enable us to invest in service improvements for products priced above $50 by improving your returns experience, reducing missing inventory, and processing faster removals.
